A flood control "ghost project" is defined as an egregious scheme of corruption — commonly plotted and executed in tandem by a Congressman, District Engineer and Contractor — involving ridiculously overpriced, substandard or non-existent infrastructure projects.

Of the three positions, the corrupt Congressman usually ends up stealing the most because he controls the terms.

There have P1.9 trillion in flood control projects spent in the last 10 years — that would have been enough money to lift the poorest Filipinos above the poverty line and into socioeconomic demographic D, and then lift half of D into the middle class. It would've been enough money to provide free Wi-Fi access to every remote mountain, farm, forest and beach across all 7,000 islands; end all homelessness in Visayas and Mindanao; AND tap Elon Musk's Boring Company to fix our world-famous traffic crisis along Edsa by building a multitude of underground high-speed tunnels, as Musk did so efficiently in Los Angeles.

A "ghost project" means that not only was there corruption that happened in terms of under-the-table cuts and kickbacks. It means that our money was stolen and then zero work was done. Literally ZERO. 

A "ghost project" means that more work was put into this clownish cardboard barrier than into an actual government project each costing tens or hundreds of millions of our taxes — and that 100% of that money was pocketed by the Cong, DE and contractor.

Not 10%. Not 25%. Not half.

All of it.
